paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: : Linguistic and geographic trends over time in harmful language research. Notably, the number of datasets for the non-top five languages continues to be lower than all English ones, while since 2017 we see more and more datasets in languages other than English.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the annual number of datasets related to harmful language research from 2012 to 2022, categorized by language, with a logarithmic y-axis ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100) datasets. The x-axis represents the year, while the legend identifies six language categories: English (blue), All other (orange), Arabic (green), Bengali (red), Spanish (purple), and Russian (brown). From 2012 to 2015, only English-language datasets are present, each with 1–4 datasets per year. In 2016, “All other” languages appear with 4 datasets, while English remains at 10. Starting in 2017, non-English datasets become more prominent: Arabic (5), Bengali (1), and Spanish (6) emerge, alongside English (20) and “All other” (15). In 2018, English peaks at ~30, “All other” at ~12, Arabic at ~6, and Bengali at 1. By 2019, English reaches ~40, “All other” ~20, Arabic ~6, Spanish ~6, and Russian ~6. In 2020, English hits ~90, “All other” ~90, Arabic ~7, Bengali ~5, Spanish ~10, and Russian ~9. In 2021, English peaks again at ~100, “All other” at ~50, Arabic ~15, Bengali ~13, Spanish ~11, and Russian ~9. In 2022, English drops to ~15, “All other” rises to ~20, Arabic falls to ~5, Spanish is absent, and Russian drops to 1. The chart visually confirms the caption’s claim that non-English datasets have grown since 2017, though English still dominates overall, and “All other” languages often surpass individual non-English languages in dataset volume.
